## Purpose

Prepare legacy completion history for strict Git containment before activation.
Preview lists source identities, strict/legacy comparisons, retained refs,
configuration and writer fences. Each equivalent-only completion needs an
explicit evidence-bearing disposition or a separately reviewed reconstruction.

## When a playbook uses it

This command is local-operator only. Worker, supervisor, service and playbook
principals cannot authorize cutover. Playbooks may direct the operator to its
preview, then continue only after the separately approved rollout gates.

## How it works internally

The CommandHandler invokes `ContainmentCutover` in
`src/integration/containment_cutover.py`. It collects repository-scoped database
facts and a disposable Git snapshot, compares strict ancestry with the old
evaluator, and binds them to the plan digest. Apply repeats the observation,
retains original objects, checks remote state again, then fences stopped writers
and the configuration generation in one bounded database transaction.

## Side effects and persistence

Preview has no durable mutations. Apply adds immutable provenance refs as
needed, inserts one bounded audit into the reserved
`integration.containment-cutover.v1:` namespace in `system_config`, and increments
the project's integration configuration generation. An identical applied plan
is repeatable while its database facts remain current. The audit survives archive
and restart; later completion generations cannot inherit the exclusion. This
command prepares history and leaves strict publisher activation to later gates.
Existing admission and watchdog paths honor only the exact approved exclusions;
selection metrics count them separately from delivered work.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`blocked` returns the manifest's per-row reasons: stop active writers, recover
missing original objects, or supply reviewed equivalence evidence before another
preview. Reconstruction remains blocked until a normal reviewed merge establishes
ancestry. `refused` covers a stale digest/configuration, changed refs or protection,
unavailable fences, malformed audit, or a second conflicting cutover. Re-preview
and resolve the named cause; never reset target heads or fabricate receipts.
Preserve retention refs after a failed apply. An incompatible rollback remains
paused and fixes forward, as described in `docs/specs/design/containment-cutover.md`.

## Operator example

Inspect the initial preview, create `choices.json` keyed by the reported completion
IDs, then save and review the preview that binds those choices:

```bash
aq integration cutover-containment --project PROJECT --json
aq integration cutover-containment --project PROJECT --choices choices.json --json > plan.json
aq integration cutover-containment --project PROJECT --plan plan.json --digest REVIEWED_SHA256 --apply
```

A `delivered_by_other_means` choice names `source_oid`, `carrying_oid`,
`equivalence_proof` (the preview's `legacy_reason`), and a nonempty `evidence`
explanation. It retires that exact delivery obligation and never proves ancestry.
